# Compression and Model Efficiency

Also called: Low-rank NeRF, Tensor Train NeRF, CCNeRF, ADMM NeRF

## Overview
This family addresses the excessive memory footprint and computational cost of standard [Neural Radiance Fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) ([NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md)) by reducing model size through low-rank approximations, tensor decompositions, and pruning. It differs from sibling methods that modify architecture for specific tasks (e.g., [Binary Radiance Fields](13622-binary-radiance-fields.md) or [Mip-NeRF 360 MLP Architecture](14098-mip-nerf-360-mlp-architecture.md)) by focusing strictly on compressing the existing radiance field representation while preserving rendering quality.

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves approximating high-dimensional parameters (typically fully connected layer weights in the MLP renderer or the radiance field tensor itself) using low-rank structures. This reduces the number of trainable parameters from $O(N^2)$ or $O(N^3)$ to $O(N \cdot r)$ or $O(N \cdot r^2)$, where $r$ is the target rank. The rendering equation remains standard volume rendering [S1], but the query function $\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \rightarrow (\sigma, \mathbf{c})$ is computed via decomposed components rather than a dense MLP.

## Subtopics

### [CCNeRF](15008-ccnerf.md)
A hybrid tensor rank [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md) method that models the radiance field *only* with tensor components, avoiding MLPs in the rendering path to preserve low-rank properties. It supports dynamic model size adjustment via [rank truncation](#7540-truncated-tensor-decomposition.md) and arbitrary composition via rank concatenation. Choose this when you need a purely tensor-based representation that allows for [scene composition](#11397-scene-composition.md) and dynamic [compression](#4-compression.md) without retraining.

### [Low Rank NeRF Approximation with ADMM](18163-low-rank-nerf-approximation-with-admm.md)
This method reduces the model size of a trained NeRF by decomposing fully connected layer weights into a Tensor Train (TT) format. It solves the resulting rank-constrained optimization problem using the [Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers](#10107-admm-solver.md) ([ADMM](#10811-l1-shearlet-regularized-ct-reconstruction-admm.md)) to minimize reconstruction error while enforcing low-rank structure. It is distinguished from sibling methods like [CCNeRF](15008-ccnerf.md) by its specific use of ADMM for rank-constrained weight decomposition rather than other compression or clustering techniques.

### PackNet with NeRF
#### definition
- [S1] A pruning-based continual learning approach applied to NeRF for multiple scenes.
#### parameter
- [S1] Pruning rate: 0.5.

## Background
The motivation for compression arises from the quadratic or cubic scaling of NeRF parameters with respect to network depth and width. Early works like [NSVF](#7144-neural-sparse-voxel-fields-nsvf.md) [MST*21] and TensoRF [CLBL22] explored hybrid tensor-MLP approaches. [CCNeRF](#15008-ccnerf.md) [S1] was introduced to provide a purely tensor-based alternative that avoids the MLP bottleneck, enabling better composition and truncation. The ADMM-based approach [S1] addresses the difficulty of directly optimizing low-rank constraints by using augmented Lagrangian methods. PackNet [ML18] was adapted to NeRF [S1] for continual learning scenarios, demonstrating that pruning can maintain performance across multiple scenes.
